correctness.rationale: For arbitrary measurable X, closed convexification preserves every directional width and can only increase area. A minimizing-width direction gives an orthogonal bounding rectangle of sides omega(X) and at most D(Omega), proving A(X)<=omega(X)D(Omega). For sharpness, a diameter segment and any interior point off its line form a triangle whose thin parallel slices have exactly linear section length, giving a sequence with ratio tending to 1/D(Omega). If equality were attained, equality in the bounding-rectangle chain would force a positive-width rectangle with one side D(Omega), whose diagonal is larger than D(Omega), a contradiction.

value.rationale: The result completely resolves one of the three replacement-functionals explicitly proposed in a published geometry paper, for every planar convex ambient body rather than for a special shape. It identifies a simple exact invariant, 1/D(Omega), proves universal nonattainment, and explains the degenerating geometry through diameter-adjacent thin slices. This is a substantive boundary result: the minimal-width variant behaves qualitatively differently from the ordinary Cheeger problem, where convex domains have attained minimizers.
